items.title: Gucci Sales Disappoint on China Slump as Turnaround Falters
items.summary: Bloomberg reports Gucci's Q3 2026 comparable sales fell 6%, worse than the 3.3% decline analysts expected, with Kering failing to reiterate its 2026 return-to-growth guidance. Coverage notes the US market, which had been offsetting China weakness earlier in the year, has also lost momentum, undercutting Kering CEO Luca de Meo's turnaround narrative for institutional and retail investors in North America.

items.title: Kering ADRs slide 12% as Gucci sales fall 6% despite in-line group revenue
items.summary: Kering shares (and US-traded ADRs) dropped about 12% after Q3 2026 results showed Gucci revenue down 4% reported / 6% comparable to EUR1.29 billion, with direct-retail sales down 9%. North America was called Gucci's 'most resilient' market with improved conversion and ticket size, but wholesale's 45% jump came off a depressed prior-year base, tempering the positive read for US investors.

items.title: Gucci to close its Meatpacking District flagship in New York
items.summary: Crain's reports Gucci is closing its roughly 9,000-square-foot Meatpacking District store on West 14th Street, putting the space on the market, as part of Kering's broader store-rationalization push. Included here because the closure is still actively cited in this week's (Oct 22-24) Q3 earnings coverage as context for North America's retail footprint -- pooled under the live earnings story rather than as a standalone stale item.

items.title: Gucci sales fell 6% as Kering raises store-closure target to at least 125
items.summary: RetailBoss (Substack-style aggregator, cross-checked against the Bloomberg/Investing.com primary wires above) reports Kering raised its full-year 2026 net store-closure target to at least 125 after already closing 105 net locations through September, with North America's most resilient-market framing offset by continued footprint cuts. Figures corroborated against T1 wires per source-pool verification_required handling.

items.title: Borbonese names Gucci veteran Marie-Laure Lequain as CEO
items.summary: WWD reports Italian handbag brand Borbonese has hired longtime Gucci executive Marie-Laure Lequain as its new CEO, a neutral personnel/talent-flow story that is factual rather than evaluative -- logged as a plain mention rather than sentiment-bearing, but relevant to NA trade readership tracking Gucci executive departures.

Purely descriptive activation coverage (what it is, who stars, where shot) with no independent evaluative verdict -- logged as brand-marketing-output, sentiment-neutral per the activation-coverage discount.

items.title: McKenna Grace wears archival and new Gucci on Hunger Games press tour

Celebrity-dressing placement coverage, descriptive rather than evaluative of the brand itself -- neutral mention, though it signals continued NA red-carpet/press-tour visibility for the house.

items.title: Gucci v. Gilt lawsuit puts luxury off-price sourcing and authentication under scrutiny
items.summary: Trade legal press covers Gucci's New York federal lawsuit against Rue Gilt Groupe/Gilt/Rue La La alleging the off-price e-commerce sites knowingly sold counterfeit Gucci Horsebit 1955 and GG Marmont Mini bags purchased by Gucci's own investigators in 2025; Gucci seeks injunctive relief and treble damages. Counterfeit/authentication controversy is a critical-angle signal directly relevant to NA off-price retail channels.

items.title: Independent fashion commentary: "Gucci Has Lost the Plot. But What If It Works?"
items.summary: An independent fashion-commentary Substack argues Gucci under Demna has abandoned the romantic maximalism of the Michele era for a flattened, influencer-coded streetwear aesthetic with deliberately sloppy tailoring and cheap-looking materials, while conceding the strategic bet might still pay off commercially.
